newsitem.title: USA: Delta earnings soar in latest quarter.
newsitem.headline: Delta earnings soar in latest quarter.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc., the latest major airline to report strong earnings, said Thursday its profits increased 79 percent in the recent quarter.
The third-ranked U.S. airline reported $125 million in net income, or $1.66 a share, for its fiscal second quarter, its third straight quarter of record earnings.
The latest results compared with $70 million, or 93 cents a share, in profits in the year-ago quarter.
The earnings topped the consensus industry analyst forecast of $1.40 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst predictions.
Delta, based in Atlanta, reported operating revenues of $3.2 billion vs. $2.9 billion in 1995's December quarter.
Delta's stock gained $1.50 to $84.25 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
On Tuesday, Continental Airlines Inc. and Northwest Airlines Corp. reported strong quarterly profits despite intense competition and sharply higher fuel prices.

"While our outstanding results for the quarter benfited from a strong economy, it was equally important that Delta also made fundamental improvements in our ability to control costs and create revenues," Chairman Ronald Allen said in a statement.

The company said revenues per seat, a measure of airline performance, rose 2.3 percent from the year-ago quarter while costs per seat rose 1 percent. Delta attributed the higher costs to a 25 percent rise in fuel prices. It said that without the price increase, costs would have declined 2.5 percent.

For the calendar year, Delta earned $754 million, or $11.11 per share, a 48 percent increase over the $510 million, or $8.26 a share, it made in calendar 1995. The 1996 results included $829 million in pretax restructuring and other one-time charges.

"The results for calendar year 1996 were the best financial performance in Delta's history for any calander or fiscal year," Allen said. "Delta is beginning to demonstrate the earnings power in this company."
